relationship: Changing gap width relative to wavelength changes diffraction spread, so controlled comparisons and equal gap-to-wavelength ratios explain the shape of outgoing wavefronts.

learnerLoop.action: Predict and test narrowing the gap at fixed wavelength, then increasing wavelength at fixed gap, and build a matching-spread case.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Gap and wavelength determine the ratio and the modelled outgoing wavefront spread.
learnerLoop.evidence: Animated wavefronts, spread indicators, reference comparisons and ratio working reveal the consequence.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Use the evidence to explain which change increased spread and construct another pair with the same ratio.

invariants: Controlled comparisons keep one quantity fixed so the cause of changing spread is visible.
Smaller gap-to-wavelength ratios yield greater spread; equal ratios give matching spread in the model.
Incoming and outgoing wavelength remain consistent in the same medium; the display is a teaching model rather than an exact wave-field measurement.
safeAdaptations: Change numeric examples and guidance while preserving separate-variable tests and ratio comparison.
Add prediction or explanation prompts grounded in the displayed wavefront evidence.
nonGoals: Do not turn the model into a quantitative diffraction-intensity measurement or a double-slit interference lab.
